content.confidence: 4: You are confident in your assessment, but not absolutely certain. It is unlikely, but not impossible, that you did not understand some parts of the submission or that you are unfamiliar with some pieces of related work.
content.summary_of_the_paper: This paper introduces a predictor-based strategy for neural architecture search. At the core of the proposed method lies the idea of using an estimated performance score as input to the predictor. This score is obtained by partial training of the architectures. Other techniques are introduced to improve the performance of the proposed method, such as a node self-attention module, a ranking strategy for the search space, and a batch sampling technique.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strengths:
- Developing better predictor-based NAS strategies is of interest to the community.
- The new Tiny-NanoBench search space could be interesting to the community.
- The experiments show that the method outperforms a naive predictor.

Weaknesses:

1) Writing quality:
The paper is poorly written and in part difficult to follow. This is clearly below the ICLR standards. 

2) Methodology:

2.1) In Section 3.1, the authors mention that they use the first three losses as estimation code. What does this mean? The first three loss terms (if so, what are these loss terms)? The loss values after the first three epochs (if so, this would suggest a vector, but Figure 1 and Figure 8 show the estimation code as a single value)? This needs to be clarified, as this is the main component of the method.

2.2) I am not really convinced by the proposed estimation code. In fact, what Figure 1 (a) shows is that architectures with the same estimation code can have significantly different ground-truth accuracies (between around 0.87 and 0.92 for an estimation code of 0.3). This means that the code is not quite a good accuracy predictor.

2.3) The goal of Equation 1 is not clear to me. This seems to rather state assumptions made by the authors, or constraints that they would like to impose, not represent the problem that they are solving. $M$ is not clearly defined, and neither is the form of the output of $g()$ and $p()$.

2.4) The choice of the placement of NSAM is justified neither by intuition nor empirically.

2.5) The text explaining the siamese ranking strategy is not very clear (although the algorithm helps).

2.6) The batch top sampling strategy seems quite standard. How does it differ from what existing methods do to sample architectures?

3) Experiments:

3.1) The parameter $c$ in siamese ranking is stated to be "an essential parameter of this algorithm". As such, I recommend the authors to evaluate its influence.

3.2) The naive predictor is not clearly defined. Furthermore, I would strongly recommend the authors to evaluate a baseline consisting of the naive predictor + NSAM and/or BTS. This would really show the benefits of the estimation code, if any.

3.3) The authors evaluate a version of their methods without BTS. It is not clear to me how it works, as one still needs to sample architectures.

3.4) The gap w.r.t. BRP-NAS is quite small. Considering that BRP-NAS can achieve a similar accuracy with only 25 samples, I would tend to favor it.

3.5) In Section 4.1.1, the authors argue and show empirically that fixing $K$ and increasing $N$ is better than fixing $N$ and increasing $K$ as done in existing methods. Therefore, it seems critical to evaluate a version of BRP-NAS that follows this strategy (it is mentioned to follow the fixed $N$ one). If it obtains the same boost as that showed in Figure 6, then it would outperform the proposed method.

4) Related work:
I understand that the authors focus the discussion on predictor-based methods, but I would nonetheless encourage them to also discuss other techniques. This would better place their method in the state of the art. For example, DARTS-based approaches are not even mentioned, although they constitute an important part of the literature.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib: As mentioned in the Weakness part, the paper is not well written and in part not clear. As such, it would be very difficult to reproduce from the text only (but the authors mention providing the source code). There are some novel components in the proposed method, albeit not of great originality.
content.summary_of_the_review: he topic studied in this paper is of interest to the community, and the proposed method has some novel components. However, the writing quality and clarity is well below the ICLR standards, and many important experiments are missing to truly demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method.
content.correctness: 3: Some of the paper’s claims have minor issues. A few statements are not well-supported, or require small changes to be made correct.
content.technical_novelty_and_significance: 3: The contributions are significant and somewhat new. Aspects of the contributions exist in prior work.
content.empirical_novelty_and_significance: 2: The contributions are only marginally significant or novel.

content.confidence: 3: You are fairly confident in your assessment. It is possible that you did not understand some parts of the submission or that you are unfamiliar with some pieces of related work. Math/other details were not carefully checked.
content.summary_of_the_paper: The paper studies performance prediction in neural architecture search. Instead of directly predicting the accuracy of a candidate network from its features, the authors propose to add a siamese branch which takes in the "Estimation Code" (early-stage training loss of the candidate network).
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strengths: 
- Reduced the cost of performance estimation is NAS (Table 1);
- Achieved a better performance prediction on NAS-Bench201 (Figure 5).
- Code is released (but I did not check whether the results are reproducible).

Weaknesses:
- The paper is extremely hard to read. Several key concepts in this paper (e.g. "Estimation Code", "Siamese Ranking", "Batch Top Sampling") sound very confusing to me. The transitions in this paper is also not very smooth.
- The authors did not compare the proposed method with other baselines in the entire experiment section and only shows that the proposed method is better than the single-stream predictor (which only takes in the architecture features).
- The authors only showed the effectiveness of the proposed method on very small scale NAS problems (e.g. CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100). Indeed, there are predictor-based NAS methods on large-scale datasets such as ImageNet. For example, the author can have a look at the Once-for-All networks (ICLR'20) which uses a very simple MLP-based predictor and works pretty well on ImageNet. I am curious whether the proposed predictor can outperform the simple predictor in OFA.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib:
- The paper is poorly written and is very hard to read.
- The experiment quality is poor, no comparison with contemporary methods are found and no ImageNet results are present in this paper.
- I cannot judge the novelty of this paper because the authors did not even show me that the proposed method can work on some real world datasets.
- The reproducibility should be good, since the authors have included the code as suggested in the paper.
content.summary_of_the_review: Considering all the weaknesses I mentioned in my review, I believe that this paper is definitely not even close to a publishable state at ICLR 2023.
content.correctness: 2: Several of the paper’s claims are incorrect or not well-supported.
content.technical_novelty_and_significance: 1: The contributions are neither significant nor novel.
content.empirical_novelty_and_significance: 1: The contributions are neither significant nor novel.

content.confidence: 3: You are fairly confident in your assessment. It is possible that you did not understand some parts of the submission or that you are unfamiliar with some pieces of related work. Math/other details were not carefully checked.
content.summary_of_the_paper: To train a predictor which estimates the final performance of a given neural architecture requires a lot of training samples. To overcome such training efficiency issue, this work propose the Estimation Code, which is a prior knowledge utilizing the relationship between the early losses of the architecture training procedure and the final accuracy. They also propose Siamese-Ranking method and Batch Top sampling. Finally, this work introduces Tiny-NanoBench as a new benchmark to validate NAS methods to design lightweight CNN architectures. This work validated the proposed method on the Tiny-NanoBench, by learning the predictor with just a few trained samples and searching for lightweight CNN architecture.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
- Strengths 
    - This work improves the sample efficiency to train the performance predictor which is widely used in NAS process.
    - This work propose the benchmark that is helpful to focus on the exploration of lightweight CNN architecture.

- Weakness
    - The first main concern is that writing is unclaer for the reviewer. I know that the clarity of the writing usually is not the main rejection reason. However, due to the lack of clear and detailed explanation of the method, it is the difficult to understand what the method is and what is the main difference compared with existing methods overally.
        - For example, in the Section 3.1 Estimation Code, the reviewer can not understand what Estimation Code exactly is. Is Estimation Code an embedding which contains the information about the architecture? If so, what is the specific prior knowledge encoded in the embedding? The reviewer guesses that it is the initial accuracy obtained after training 3 epochs of each architecture.
        - What is the key contribution that Tiny-NanoBench has better computational efficient architectures compared with Tiny-NASBench-201? 
    - The second concern is a novelty issue. After reading the paper, the reviewer get the impression that the proposed method is to combine the broadly used techniques instead of proposing new method or addressing the challenging issues.
        - For example, using initial accuracy as proxy for architecture has been widely used for sampling-based NAS methods. Compared with the existing sampling-based NAS methods, what is the advatage of the Estimation Code?
        - The proposed Batch top sampling (BTS) looks similar with WeakNAS[1], which selects training top n samples progressively.

[1] Stronger NAS with Weaker Predictors, NeurIPS 2021.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib:
As I mentioned in Strength and Weaknesses section, I believe that the clarity and quality of this work need to be improved. 
The reproducibility of this work is well explained as the authors added the detailed descriptions for the reproducibility at the implementational level.
content.summary_of_the_review: While this work shows good training sampling efficiency to train the predictor, the method description is rather unclear and the reviewer believe that the contributions are marginal compared with the previous NAS works.
content.correctness: 3: Some of the paper’s claims have minor issues. A few statements are not well-supported, or require small changes to be made correct.
content.technical_novelty_and_significance: 2: The contributions are only marginally significant or novel.
content.empirical_novelty_and_significance: 2: The contributions are only marginally significant or novel.
